migrationTarget.targetFact: WWC_SERVER_AUTH_SUBJECT is replaced by UserAccountService-owned UserAccount identities; browser sessions reference a durable userId instead of a process environment value.

risks: The subject value is consumed in four independent places (bootstrap actor, model authority, admission identity, enterprise identity); each consumer must switch to the authenticated session user without changing model-route or admission semantics.

Phase 1 task 8 explicitly requires migrating the existing fixed subject; a one-time migration must create an Owner UserAccount whose userId keeps public projections stable or every recorded audit/actor fact changes meaning.
Startup currently fails fast when the variable is missing; removing it changes the documented startup contract in crates/winwincode-server/README.md and every vertical script at once.

migrationTarget.targetFact: The single repository root becomes registered ClientNodes each carrying RepositoryBindings; RepositoryBinding identities and security metadata live in Control Plane while absolute paths stay in Device Client local storage.

risks: Compatibility window may map the legacy WWC_SERVER_REPOSITORY_ROOT onto one built-in Local Client projection, but the two semantics must not coexist long term; the removal step must be a named, gated migration.

crates/winwincode-server/tests/application_composition.rs asserts the literal variable name inside main.rs source text, so any rename or removal must update that source-text contract in the same change.

WWC_SERVER_SOURCE_ROOT is derived from the repository root today (main.rs lines 123-130); multi-repository scheduling must define where execution source roots come from once the Server no longer owns absolute paths.

RepositoryScope (organization/workspace/project/repository IDs) is currently one fixed set of environment values; Registry/ACL migration must define how these IDs relate to RepositoryBinding identities.

The Client login page, HTTP contract security scheme, and all browser verticals are built around this one-proof flow.

migrationTarget.targetFact: The bootstrap proof becomes a one-time initialization credential: an uninitialized Server accepts exactly one proof to create the first Owner user, then bootstrap initialization closes permanently; daily sign-in uses username plus Argon2id password.

risks: Today the proof configures a session for a fixed subject on every start; after migration it must be accepted only once per Server lifetime and then permanently disabled, which invalidates the current restart-and-reuse bootstrap behavior covered by auth_session.rs restart tests.

apps/client login form, the generated HTTP contract bootstrapProof security scheme, and several browser leak-prevention tests encode the proof semantics; all must move to username/password without weakening the write-only, never-echoed guarantees.

Login rate limiting, session TTL renewal, logout, and disable-user-revokes-sessions (plan section 10.2) have no current equivalents; the existing cookie/session primitives must be extended rather than replaced.

migrationTarget.targetFact: The endpoint and transport stay unchanged; per plan section 22.3 the exchange gains Worker Session Credential validation and WorkerLaunchGrant verification (clientNodeId, occupancyLeaseId, fencing token, workerSessionId) before registration succeeds.

risks: The current credential is a static shared file with no binding to a ClientNode, occupancy lease, or workerSession; adding LaunchGrant checks must reject stale or cross-tenant launches without breaking existing ExecutionPort parity tests.

Registration currently proves only possession of one file plus one remote-worker subject/expiry tuple; the admission identity path (main.rs line 326 with_admission_identity) must learn about managed-session credentials.
Any error-shape change on this endpoint is visible to spawned Workers in all verticals; keep frame semantics and categories stable while the credential layer changes underneath.

migrationTarget.targetFact: A second managed launch mode is added: winwincode-worker --managed-session <config-file> with a 0600 config carrying clientNodeId, occupancyLeaseId, fencing token, repositoryBindingId, workerSessionId and sourceDirectory written by the Device Client; --remote remains for standalone and test use.

risks: sourceDirectory today comes from WWC_WORKER_SOURCE_ROOT supplied by the operator; under managed launch only the Device Client may write sourceDirectory so the Server never provides absolute paths (plan section 14.4).

One WorkerSession must map to exactly one Worker process with its own PID, data root and worktree; the current env-based entry has no notion of workerSessionId, so the config file and identity plumbing are new surface area for the same binary.
All existing verticals keep using --remote; the two entry modes must share one execution kernel so managed-session behavior does not fork the execution semantics.

migrationTarget.targetFact: Browser sessions bind to a durable UserAccount (username plus Argon2id login) with TTL renewal, login rate limiting, logout, and immediate revocation of every session when the user is disabled; cookie attributes and secret-free persistence are preserved.

risks: Sessions currently authorize a fixed subject with one repository Scope; multi-user sessions must carry a real userId and be validatable against user state on every request, not only at issue time.

revoke_actor_sessions becomes the disable-user kill switch; its current per-actor semantics must extend to disabled accounts and login rate limiting without changing the WebSocket revocation-close behavior covered by tests.
Enterprise external-identity login shares the same cookie primitives; both issue paths must converge on UserAccount identities so no second session semantics appears.

migrationTarget.targetFact: Task submission first requires an occupied ClientNode and a validated RepositoryAccessGrant; ExecutionReservation gains client/repository/occupancy facts and SessionBinding extends with a local execution source (ClientNode/occupancy/worker launch facts) while keeping the current identity, replay and fencing rules.

risks: Session creation currently trusts the single fixed repository scope from startup; it must gain occupancy and repository-grant checks (Phases 4 and 5) before Phase 7 can schedule against occupied ClientNodes.

SessionBinding identity rules are exact-match today (binding.rs, product_session_service.rs); extending the identity with local execution source facts must not weaken the existing mismatch rejection paths covered by control-plane tests.

Quick Chat reuses a long-lived WorkerSession while StrongFlow attempts create new ones; the managed-session scheduler must preserve both patterns plus retry-with-new-identity semantics when the launch path moves behind the Device Client.

compatibilityRules: winwincode-local single-machine composition stays the development, test, and all-local deployment entry (plan section 22.1); it is not converted into a Device Client.
Legacy WWC_SERVER_REPOSITORY_ROOT may map onto one built-in Local Client projection during the compatibility window, but dual business semantics must not persist; removal is a named migration step.

RemoteWorkerPort and the ExecutionPort exchange transport are retained; Phase 6 adds Worker Session Credential and WorkerLaunchGrant verification instead of rewriting the transport (plan section 22.3).
The bootstrap proof remains write-only, digest-persisted, and never echoed; migration changes who may present it (uninitialized Server, exactly once) not its secrecy guarantees.

migrationOrder.rationale: Phase 1 / AUTH-100: UserAccountService and Owner bootstrap unblock every later grant, occupancy, and audit fact that must name a real user.
Phase 6 / WORKER-100 + WORKER-200: managed-session launch and LaunchGrant verification reuse today's exchange transport and can land while single-root scheduling still works.
Phase 5 / REPO-100: repository registry and ACL need Device Client local path storage, which depends on Phase 2-4; the built-in Local Client projection bridges the compatibility window.
Phase 7 / FLOW-100: session creation gains occupancy and repository-grant checks only after AUTH-100, CLIENT-300, REPO-100 and WORKER-200 facts exist; identity and replay rules stay frozen.
